scope: Physicochemical compatibility in a single syringe only. No dosing, timing, fasting, pharmacology or clinical considerations.

reason_codes.R00: No chemical conflict identified. Compatible vehicles, compatible charge, no reactive residues.
reason_codes.R01: Charge complexation. Anionic lipidated/acidic peptide + polycationic peptide forms an insoluble coacervate: haze, stringing, gel or visible precipitate. This is the classic GLP-1 + CJC-1295 'thickening'.
reason_codes.R02: Vehicle/pH mismatch. One component is only soluble or only stable in an acidic vehicle; on contact with a neutral buffered solution it drops out or the partner is acid-degraded.
reason_codes.R03: Copper-catalysed oxidation. Cu2+ oxidises Met, Trp, Tyr and His residues in the partner peptide, generating sulfoxides and cleavage products.
reason_codes.R04: Thiol-metal redox. Free thiol reduces Cu2+ to Cu+, decolourises the complex and drops copper/peptide precipitate. Irreversible.
reason_codes.R05: Disulfide reduction or scrambling. Free thiol opens a disulfide-dependent ring or cross-links cysteine-containing partners.
reason_codes.R06: Aggregation/fibril seeding. An amyloidogenic or aggregation-prone component nucleates the partner; result may be delayed (hours), not immediate.
reason_codes.R07: Co-solvent crash. Component requires DMSO/propylene glycol/ethanol; on dilution the small molecule precipitates and/or the organic solvent denatures the aqueous peptide.
reason_codes.R08: Large or glycosylated protein. Formulation excipients are load-bearing, interfacial and shear denaturation risk, aggregation is invisible until it isn't. No co-formulation data exists.
reason_codes.R09: Ionic strength / osmolarity / excipient mismatch. High-concentration amino-acid, vitamin or lipotropic blends carry preservatives, chelators and osmolarity that destabilise peptides.
reason_codes.R10: Redox cofactor instability. Cobalt-centred B12 and NAD+ are photo/redox active and accelerate degradation of oxidation-sensitive partners; NAD+ solutions are also strongly acidic.
reason_codes.R11: Acid-catalysed deamidation. GHRH-analogue Asn8/Asp cleaves and deamidates rapidly below pH 5.
reason_codes.R12: Adsorption and rapid degradation. Highly surface-active or protease-labile peptide; dilution into a mixed matrix accelerates loss.
reason_codes.R13: Not a co-administration product under any circumstances. Different route, different tissue plane, or toxin.

classes.GLP1: Lipidated incretin analogues. Anionic at neutral pH, self-assemble into micelles/oligomers, phosphate+mannitol buffered ~pH 6.5-7.5.
classes.AMYLIN: Lipidated amylin analogue. Anionic, strongly amyloidogenic.
classes.GHRH: GHRH analogues. Cationic, Asn/Asp deamidation-prone, aggregation-prone.
classes.GHS: Ghrelin-mimetic secretagogues. Small, cationic, chemically robust, Trp-bearing.
classes.MSH: Melanocortin analogues. Cationic, cyclic/lactam, Trp-bearing, robust.
classes.KHAVINSON: Short bioregulator peptides (2-4 residues). No oxidisable or reactive residues. Chemically inert.
classes.ROBUST: Small-to-mid peptides with no free thiol, no critical disulfide and no significant oxidisable residue load.
classes.OXSENS: Peptides carrying Met/Trp that are readily oxidised.
classes.ACIDIC: Requires a low-pH / acetic acid vehicle for solubility and stability.
classes.LIPOBLEND: High-volume lipotropic, amino-acid or vitamin blends.
